title: Analytics engine
description:
# Analytics engine

**Source:** Plane Pit Lane project (Backlog)

## User Story

**As a** racer, **I want** to compare my race metrics against historical data — best laps, consistency scores, improvement trends, **So that** I can make data-driven decisions about car modifications and driving strategy.

## Success Criteria

- Analytics dashboard renders with real race data from entries, scoped to the signed-in user
- Comparison works across cars, versions, tracks, and time periods via filters
- Key metrics (best lap, average lap, consistency score) computed correctly from stored runs
- Trend visualizations are readable on mobile and desktop
- AI integration point defined and documented, with queries scoped to the user's data

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dashboard showing today's events with live metrics
- Historical comparison: per-car, per-version, per-track-config
- Key metrics: best lap time, average lap time, consistency score (std dev), improvement over time
- Filter by date range, car, version, event, track config
- AI integration placeholder — future algorithms can query datasets and surface insights
- All queries scoped to the signed-in user's data

## Definition of Done
- Analytics dashboard renders with real data from race entries
- Filtering works across all dimensions
- Historical trend visualizations are readable on mobile and desktop

**Requires:** race data entry, users/ownership

title: Google sign-in
description:
# Google sign-in

**Source:** GitHub backlog breakdown, 2026-08-01

## User Story

**As a** racer, **I want** to sign in with my Google account, **So that** I can access my data without creating and remembering another password.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Scenario:** First-time sign-in creates an account
  - **Given:** I am on the login page
  - **and Given:** I have never signed in before
  - **When:** I click "Sign in with Google" and authorize the app
  - **Then:** an account is created for me and I am redirected into the app

- **Scenario:** Returning sign-in loads my data
  - **Given:** I have signed in with Google before
  - **When:** I click "Sign in with Google"
  - **Then:** I am logged into my existing account and my cars, events, and runs load

- **Scenario:** Signed-out access is blocked
  - **Given:** I am not signed in
  - **When:** I try to open an app page directly
  - **Then:** I am redirected to the login page

## Definition of Done
- Google OAuth provider configured (client ID/secret via env)
- Login page with "Sign in with Google" button
- Session persists across browser sessions
- All app routes require a signed-in user except the login page
- Logout available
- New users get a `users` row via the users card; existing users map back to their account

**Requires:** users/ownership, hosting/deployment (live URL for OAuth callback)
**Blocks:** settings (per-user)

title: Car photos
description:
# Car photos

**Source:** Designer mockup review, 2026-08-05

## User Story

**As a** racer, **I want** to upload a photo of each of my cars and see it displayed alongside that car, **So that** I can visually identify my cars at a glance in the interface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Scenario:** Upload image to a car
  - **Given:** I have a car registered in the app
  - **When:** I upload an image on that car's page
  - **Then:** the image is saved and associated with that specific car

- **Scenario:** View car image
  - **Given:** a car has an uploaded image
  - **When:** I view the car in the list or detail view
  - **Then:** the image is displayed alongside the car

- **Scenario:** Replace image
  - **Given:** a car already has an image
  - **When:** I upload a new image for that car
  - **Then:** the new image replaces the old one

- **Scenario:** Remove image
  - **Given:** a car has an image
  - **When:** I remove the image
  - **Then:** the image is deleted and the car shows no image / placeholder

- **Scenario:** Image persists across devices
  - **Given:** I upload an image
  - **When:** I sign in from a different device
  - **Then:** the image is still there (per-account, NOT per-device)

## Storage decision (OPEN — resolve before implementation)

Requirements: must be **per-account** and persist across devices. Candidate options:

- **Object storage (Vercel Blob or S3-compatible)** — preferred. Vercel Hobby serverless has no persistent filesystem; Blob/S3 fits the existing deploy target. Store the object's URL in the DB (Turso). Per-account, cross-device.
- **Database BLOB (Turso)** — possible but not preferred: bloats DB and edge replication for photos. Only viable for tiny images.
- **File share / server filesystem** — NOT viable: Vercel serverless functions have no persistent filesystem.
- **LocalStorage** — REJECTED: per-device, not per-account; images would not follow the user across devices.

Also determine: is image transformation (resize/thumbnail) needed at upload time, serve time, or both?

## Definition of Done
- Car page has upload control (signed-in only)
- Image persists per-account, not per-device
- Image displays in car list and car detail per the designer mockup
- Replace and remove supported; orphaned files cleaned up
- Storage matches the chosen option above; schema updated if storing URLs/BLOBs (Drizzle migration, schema conventions)
- `vp check` and `vp test` pass

**Requires:** car CRUD (done), users/ownership (for per-account scoping)
**Blocks:** — (none; visual polish / feature enhancement, not on the MVP critical path)

title: E2E coverage for the real app stack
description:
# E2E coverage for the real app stack

## Context

Current Playwright suite (`tests/`) runs only against the static HTML mock
(`scripts/serve-mocked-ui.mjs`) — no DB, no SSR, no real API. It proves the mock UI
behavior contract but never exercises the real app (routes, server functions, Drizzle).

## Goal

Add a second e2e suite that runs the **real app** in CI:
- Build with `vp build` (nitro preset: vercel)
- Serve locally via nitro preview (or a dev server) on a test port
- Point Playwright at the real app with a **local test DB** (the existing `local.db` /
  Drizzle local file path, or a scratch DB) so requests hit real server functions
- Assert real behaviors: car CRUD through the UI, event/run entry, validation errors

## Decision needed

Scope of "real stack" for CI:
- Full SSR app + real API against a local test DB (recommended, high value)
- Or add `vercel dev` local-slice e2e later, run manually on the dev machine
  (needs Vercel login + linked project + TURSO_* env — impractical in CI)

## Acceptance criteria

- `vp test:e2e` (or a new script) runs the real-app suite in CI and passes
- Existing static-mock suite still passes (both coexist)
- No Vercel login / no real secrets required in CI
- Docs updated (README / docs) describing the two e2e suites

## Definition of done

- New e2e config or suite file covering real routes against a local test DB
- CI job runs both suites
- `vp check` and `vp test` pass

title: Vercel deployment polish
description:
# Vercel deployment polish

**Source:** GitHub backlog breakdown, 2026-08-01

## What

Replace the token+CLI deploy interface with the Vercel GitHub App integration:
- Install the Vercel GitHub App on the repo, link the project to the shared Vercel Team
- `vercel.json` gains `buildCommand: "vp build"` (framework hint: nitro)
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` becomes obsolete and is removed
- Push to main → Vercel builds + deploys production; PRs → preview deployments automatically

## Why (vs the current token+CLI path)

- No CI token to provision/rotate — auth comes from GitHub repo access (cleanest fit for "both partners deploy via git push")
- Free preview deployments for PRs without a second workflow
- Less secret-management surface (only runtime env vars stay in Vercel)

## Acceptance (when picked up)

- GitHub App installed with repo access; project linked to team
- Main push deploys prod; PR opens a preview URL
- deploy.yml removed; token-based secrets no longer required in CI

title: Users and data ownership
description:
# Users and data ownership

**Source:** Plane Pit Lane project (Backlog)

## User Story

**As a** racer using the hosted app, **I want** my cars, events, and runs scoped to my account, **So that** my data stays private and never mixes with other racers'.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Scenario:** New user's data is isolated
  - **Given:** I have a user account
  - **and Given:** I have created cars, events, and runs
  - **When:** another user signs in
  - **Then:** they cannot see, edit, or delete any of my data

- **Scenario:** Existing data gets an owner
  - **Given:** the app has data recorded before users existed
  - **When:** the ownership migration runs
  - **Then:** every existing car, event, and run is assigned to the original owner

- **Scenario:** API scopes by owner
  - **Given:** I am signed in
  - **When:** I call any list or detail API
  - **Then:** I only receive rows owned by me

## Definition of Done
- `users` table in schema (user_id PK, email, google_sub, display_name, created_at)
- `user_id` FK on `cars`, `events`, `runs` (snapshots inherit via cars)
- Migration assigns existing rows to the seed/first user
- All server APIs (cars, events, runs) filter by `user_id`
- Tests updated for ownership scoping; existing tests still pass

**Requires:** schema design (done)
**Blocks:** Google sign-in, settings, analytics
